title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (end of the Pic discussion from p.180). X/S is proper, and X^{(p/S)} is the Frobenius twist. The map Pic_{X^{(p)}/S} = Pic_{X/S}^{(p)} -> Pic_{X/S} has been identified (admitted) with the Verschiebung V. This page draws the consequence. The homomorphism it induces on Lie algebras, Lie(Pic)^{(p)} -> Lie(Pic), i.e. R^1f_*O_{X^{(p)}} -> R^1f_*O_X, is the p-th power operation of the restricted (p-)Lie algebra. Grothendieck asks whether this is in Demazure-Gabriel. Its transpose, on f_*Omega^1 (via duality), is the Cartier operation on differential forms. This is the Hasse-Witt/Cartier duality picture.

Section (7), the smooth case of relative dimension one: 'a remarkable pairing'. Hypothesis: Omega^1_{X/S} (= Omega^1_{X/X^{(p)}}) is locally free of rank 1. Equivalently, X has locally a one-element relative p-basis {x}, so F_{X/S}: X -> X^{(p)} is finite locally free of degree p. Put Lambda = O_{X^{(p)}} and Q = F_*O_X / Lambda. Q is locally free of rank p-1 over Lambda (basis x, ..., x^{p-1}).

Grothendieck defines a canonical Lambda-bilinear pairing Q x Q -> Omega^1_{X^{(p)}/S} (tensored over Lambda). Equivalently, it is a form phi on F_*O_X that vanishes when either argument lies in Lambda.

The next page completes this:
- phi(f,g) = C(f dg), with C the Cartier operator.
- phi is Lambda-bilinear, and it vanishes when f or g lies in Lambda because C kills exact forms.
- phi is skew: alternating for p odd, symmetric for p = 2.
- It is a perfect duality. The matrix in the basis x^i is anti-diagonal with entries j, so the determinant is ±(p-1)! = ∓1 in F_p^* (Wilson).
- Corollary: Q ≅ Q^vee ⊗ Omega^1_{X^{(p)}/S}, hence det Q ≅ det Q^vee ⊗ (Omega^1)^{⊗(p-1)}, i.e. (det Q)^{⊗2} ≅ omega^{⊗(p-1)}.

In modern terms, d identifies Q with B^1 = d(F_*O_X), the sheaf of locally exact 1-forms. This is the classical self-duality of B^1 on a curve in characteristic p, here stated relatively over an arbitrary base S under only the 'rank-one p-basis' hypothesis.
errors: The page says Q is 'loc. libre de rang p-1 sur S'. It is locally free of rank p-1 over Lambda = O_{X^{(p)}}, not over S.

Next page: the vanishing condition for C(x^i d x^j) = C(j x^{i+j-1} dx) is written as 'i+j ≠ p-1'. It should be 'i+j ≠ p'. The nonzero case is i+j-1 = p-1, which matches the anti-diagonal matrix that is drawn.
Next page: 'f dg + g df = d(fg) = 0' should read 'is exact, hence killed by C'.
For p=2 the form is symmetric and not alternating (phi(x,x) = C(x dx) = dx' ≠ 0), as Grothendieck correctly notes. The phrase 'antisymétrique' must be read as 'skew', i.e. phi(f,g) + phi(g,f) = 0.

ideas.what: The Lie-algebra map induced by Verschiebung on Pic is the p-power operation of the restricted Lie algebra; its transpose is the Cartier operator (Hasse-Witt).
ideas.modern_name: Lie(V) = p-map; Hasse-Witt matrix dual to Cartier operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1958, Mexico), Cartier; Oda (1969); Demazure-Gabriel (1970) for V vs p-map
ideas.where_published: Demazure-Gabriel, Groupes algébriques; Oda, Ann. Sci. ENS 1969; Katz, Publ. IHES 39 (1970)

ideas.what: Canonical perfect skew pairing on Q = F_*O_X/O_{X'} ≅ B^1 with values in Omega^1_{X'/S}, given by (f,g) ↦ C(f dg), for relative dimension one with a one-element p-basis.
ideas.modern_name: Self-duality of the sheaf B of locally exact differentials (B ≅ B^vee ⊗ omega)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud, 'Sections des fibrés vectoriels sur une courbe' (Bull. SMF 1982); used later by Mehta-Pauly, Joshi et al.

ideas.what: Determinant identity det Q ≅ det Q^vee ⊗ omega^{p-1}, i.e. (det B^1)^2 ≅ omega^{p-1}, computed via Wilson's theorem.
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of Frobenius direct image / theta-characteristic-type relation for B

missed.claim: A relative (over arbitrary base S) version of the perfect skew Cartier pairing on F_*O_X/O_{X'} (≅ B^1), with explicit perfectness proof via Wilson's theorem. It is likely written in the 1970s, predating or contemporaneous with Raynaud's 1982 use of the self-duality of B on curves.
missed.quote: On va définir un accouplement Λ-bilinéaire canonique (*) Q×Q ⟶ Ω^1_{X^{(p)/S}/S}⊗Λ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical attribution. The pairing is well known for smooth curves over a field. The relative formulation under only the 'one-element p-basis' hypothesis is a mild generalization, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is correct and elegant, but the pairing C(f dg) on B^1, its skew/perfect nature and the determinant consequence are known (Raynaud 1982 and later work on Frobenius-destabilized bundles). The Lie(V)/p-map and Cartier/Hasse-Witt duality are classical. The only interest is an early, relative-base formulation by Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'en question induit sur Lie est l'opération des puissances p-ièmes', i.e. 'induit' (not 'inverse') and 'est' (not 'et').
Section heading: 'Cas lisse de dim relative un : un accouplement remarquable' ('lisse' inserted above, 'de la' struck out).
'Plus généralement, en dim. de dim relative 1': the word is unclear, possibly 'en cas de' or 'au lieu de'.
The final displayed map is written φ: f_{X/S*}(O_X) × f_{X/S*}(O_X) → Ω^1_{X^{(p)/S}/S} ⊗_{O_{X^{(p)/S}}} Λ; the struck-out leading Λ in (*) is correctly marked as deleted.
